blocks.text: The collection has the right skills in the wrong order. The domain vocabulary gets its final form last ([[F08]], [[F30]]), and the data model comes after every feature and screen ([[F17]]). In 3 of 4 flows, a hard gate has no upstream node that satisfies it ([[F01]], [[F02]], [[F03]]), and `check.py` does not look ([[F04]]). The editor cannot tell a finished node from the files, because no skill declares what it produces ([[F05]]). The reasons behind artifacts and the approvals stay in chat ([[F13]], [[F23]]). The review holds 44 findings: 3 critical, 13 high, 21 medium, 7 low.

items: The skills are flat: 30 skills in one directory level, and the longest ([[ops-review]]) has 111 lines.
One artifact tree holds all 14 targets, from [[a-brief]] to [[a-11_build]], so every skill writes to a known place.
`scripts/check.py` is the single gate of the collection; its flow rule has one gap ([[F04]]).
The glossary format keeps an `_Avoid_` list per term, so a rejected word has a home.
A decision enters `decisions.md` only after the three-test check.
Feature dossiers are frozen records of the reasons ([[a-08_dossiers]]).

rows.title: appbuilder-mvp cannot pass its own hard gates (stories.yaml, 07_screens)
rows.detail: `spec-featuresets` hard-gates `_concept/04_journeys/stories.yaml`, but the flow has no `experience-journeys` node. `build-plan` and `build-implement` hard-gate `_concept/07_screens`, but the flow has no `spec-feature` or `experience-shell` node. Three hard gates in this flow have no upstream writer.
rows.recommendation: Add the producing nodes to `appbuilder-mvp`, or make the three gates `soft` and say in each step what changes without the file. Add the check.py rule of F04.

rows.title: appbuilder-standard runs mockup-storybook before the tech stack it hard-gates on
rows.detail: `mockup-storybook` hard-gates `10_blueprint/techstack.md` and reads it in step 1. In `appbuilder-standard` it runs at node 12; `architecture-techstack` runs at node 15, after annotate and feedback. The gate cannot be open when the node starts.
rows.recommendation: Move `architecture-techstack` and `architecture-system` before the mockup nodes. Or gate `mockup-storybook` soft and take the framework from the template default.

rows.title: skaileup-concept-reverse runs spec-feature; nothing writes its scope.yaml gate
rows.detail: `spec-feature` hard-gates `_concept/01_meta/scope.yaml`. The reverse flow starts at `concept-reverse`, which only reads that file, and has no `concept-scope` node. When the host's profile picker starts the flow, no node writes `scope.yaml`. A grep of `skaile-forge/server` for `scope.yaml` and `01_meta` finds 0 hits, so the host writes none either.
rows.recommendation: Make `concept-scope` the entry of the reverse flow, or let `concept-reverse` write `scope.yaml` with `flow: skaileup-concept-reverse`.

rows.title: check.py never checks that a hard gate has an upstream writer
rows.detail: The docstring says a prerequisite no skill writes is raised here. `_check_one_flow` (lines 730-842) checks id, name, presentation, node ids, edge types, reachability and `requires:`. It never compares a node's hard gate with the nodes upstream, so F01 to F03 stay green. A search of check.py for writer or producer logic finds none.
rows.recommendation: Add a rule: walk each flow's `type: flow` edges, collect the targets written so far, and fail on a hard gate with no writer upstream. It needs the `produces` list of F05.

rows.title: No skill declares what it produces, so the editor cannot derive done state
rows.detail: The editor marks a node done from `contracts/artifacts.yaml` `produced_by`, and falls back to the session when none exists. This collection ships no such file: ADR 0001 records it as unreachable under a copy install, and no skill frontmatter has a `produces` key. `skaileup` step 3.2 therefore walks the tree for the first node whose artifacts are missing, with no list to look up.
rows.recommendation: Add `metadata.artifacts.produces: [{id, path}]` to every skill, checked by check.py. Ask the host to read done state from that list, as it already reads `artifacts.requires`.

rows.title: Dialog answers have two homes: host user_input.json and answers.json
rows.detail: The host stores each step's dialog input at `_concept/_grounding/<step>/user_input.json` and injects it into the prompt. The collection keeps answers at `02_grounding/onboarding/answers.json`, and a search of `skaile-forge/server` for `answers.json` finds 0 hits. Only `concept-onboard` mentions `answers.json` among the skills. The other skills' dialog values stay in the host file.
rows.recommendation: Make `concept-onboard` step 1 merge what the host handed in into `answers.json` once. Record the host path as a fact in `scripts/host_facts.py`.

rows.title: Contract volume: 13 files, 2,373 lines, cited whole
rows.detail: The 13 contracts hold 2,373 lines (README.md and CONTRACT.md excluded). `spec-feature` and `architecture-datamodel` cite 7 contracts each. `experience-shell` cites 4; two of them, `elements_block.md` (401 lines) and `walkthrough_renderer.md` (445 lines), serve one `kind: nav` element in step 6.
rows.recommendation: Cite `§` sections, as the skills already do for `agent_patterns.md`. Point `experience-shell` at `elements_block.md § Schema` and `walkthrough_renderer.md § App-shell navigation`.

rows.title: The domain glossary sits in the blueprint and is written by three skills
rows.detail: The glossary is `10_blueprint/glossary.md`. `concept-brief` writes it at node 3 of 27, `spec-feature` writes it during every feature, and `architecture-datamodel` settles it at node 17. `experience-journeys`, `spec-featuresets`, `experience-behaviors` and `experience-shell` have 0 mentions of `glossary` in their SKILL.md and references.
rows.recommendation: Put one `glossary.md` beside `brief.md`. One step writes it right after the brief; every later skill reads it.

rows.title: concept-reverse is a second writer of six artifacts
rows.detail: `concept-reverse` writes `brief.md`, `goals.md`, `comparable.md`, `10_blueprint/techstack.md`, `03_brand/identity.md` and `03_brand/tokens.json`. Their owners are `concept-brief`, `architecture-techstack` and `design-brand`. The `extraction_confidence` grades appear only in `concept-reverse`, and no owner names it.
rows.recommendation: Let `concept-reverse` write only `02_grounding/findings/*`. The owning skills read those findings as seeds.

rows.title: Competitor knowledge lives in two files
rows.detail: `concept-research` writes `02_grounding/research/competitors.md`. `concept-brief` writes `comparable.md`, a second file about the same competitor products. No rule says which file is the source.
rows.recommendation: Keep one file. Make `comparable.md` a section of `brief.md` that cites `competitors.md`.

rows.title: Screenshots have three homes
rows.detail: Screenshots go to `02_grounding/findings/`, to `02_grounding/research/step/<skill name>/` or to `03_brand/references/`. Two skills write them, and no rule picks one home.
rows.recommendation: Use `02_grounding/findings/` only, with a `step` field in `findings/index.md`.

rows.title: concept-research is "not a pipeline step" but both flows place it after brief
rows.detail: `concept-research` says it has no place in the order. `appbuilder-standard` and `skaileup-concept-only` run it right after `concept-brief`. `concept-brief` step 1 reads the research files "where research ran first", so in both flows those files do not exist yet.
rows.recommendation: Run research before brief, or delete the node and keep the "alongside" semantics.

rows.title: Approvals and choices stay in chat
rows.detail: `concept-brief` waits for a "yes in words", and `design-brand` iterates until the user approves; neither records the approval in a file. `artifact_frontmatter.md` has no `approved` field (grep: 0 hits). The monorepo choice in `concept-reverse` and the seed-table corrections in `concept-onboard` are not recorded either. The editor shows the result, never the decision.
rows.recommendation: Add `approved: <date>` to the universal frontmatter fields and write it at each approval. Record every dialog answer in `answers.json`.

rows.title: "One question per message" is restated in six skills
rows.detail: Six skills restate the rule in their own words. Five also cite `agent_patterns.md § Questions Are Standalone Messages`; `design-brand` does not.
rows.recommendation: Let the contract alone carry the rule. A skill lists only which questions it asks.

rows.title: "Unset type is web-app" is stated twice; the flow choice is described twice
rows.detail: `concept-scope` and `concept-onboard` both state that an unset project type reads as `web-app`. `concept-scope` step 4 describes how the flow is chosen, and `skaileup` describes it again and names the host's profile picker as a second chooser.
rows.recommendation: Give each fact one owner: `concept-scope` owns the `web-app` default and the flow choice, and `skaileup` only points at it.

rows.title: Onboarding answers sit in two files, stack preferences in two artifacts
rows.detail: `concept-onboard` keeps raw dialog answers in `answers.json` and the decisions with their confidence in `onboarding.yaml`, so one answer has two homes. `architecture-techstack` never reads the `locked`/`preferred`/`open` grade that `concept-onboard` says it must honour; `concept-reverse` writes `techstack.md` as a second writer (see F09).
rows.recommendation: Make `answers.json` the only record of what the user said; derive `onboarding.yaml` from it or drop it. Make `architecture-techstack` read the confidence grade in step 1.

rows.title: Gate cycle: the data model needs every feature, every feature needs the model
rows.detail: `architecture-datamodel` hard-gates `05_features` and writes `data_entities[]` back into every feature file. `spec-feature` lists `datamodel` under `requires` and soft-gates it, but no step reads the model file: step 2 only notes that its absence puts the load on the interview, and step 1 calls `data_entities:` something "later steps" populate. Both standard flows that contain the two skills run the model last, so every feature and screen is specified without a data model.
rows.recommendation: Design the data model before the features, from the journeys and the glossary. Let each feature spec read the entities it uses instead of receiving them later.

rows.title: Entity names are coined four times before any model exists
rows.detail: Journeys write `candidate_entities`, featuresets fix a role vocabulary, behaviors name entities and enum states, and feature specs list the entities each feature reads or writes. None of the four reads `glossary.md` (0 `glossary` mentions in `experience-*` and `spec-featuresets`). `architecture-datamodel` then renames its model to match the glossary.
rows.recommendation: Pin the vocabulary and the entity names first, once. Let these four skills read the names and never coin them.

rows.title: Permissions are written in four places with no owner
rows.detail: Each feature spec carries a `permissions:` block plus a restated table. Behaviors add a role × transition table, featuresets settle the role list, and the data model seeds a `permissions` scenario. The contract names the feature file as the home; the other three copies have no rule that keeps them equal.
rows.recommendation: Make the feature spec the only owner of permissions. Let behaviors, featuresets and the seed cite it.

rows.title: Acceptance criteria are written three times with no shared id
rows.detail: `experience-journeys` says its EARS lines are copied verbatim into feature specs and the ledger, but `spec-feature` says every criterion traces to the grill, and no step copies from `stories.yaml`. `build-plan` then creates a ledger row per spec criterion, and `quality-e2e` runs the criteria again from `stories.yaml`. Behaviors express the same guards as `requires`/`ensures` columns, and `architecture-datamodel` reads both with no precedence for guards.
rows.recommendation: Give each criterion one id in `stories.yaml`. Let the spec and the ledger cite the id and never retype the text.

rows.title: Two skills write an `elements:` block while the contract names one writer
rows.detail: `experience-shell` step 6 writes a `kind: nav` element into `shell.md`. `spec-feature` and `contracts/elements_block.md` both call `spec-feature` the sole writer of `elements:`; the contract never mentions the shell.
rows.recommendation: Name both writers in `elements_block.md`. Or move the nav element to `spec-feature` and let the shell write prose only.

rows.title: Scope decisions are recorded in four places
rows.detail: A cut feature appears in the featuresets cut list, in the spec's `## Out of Scope`, in the dossier's scope line and, past the three-test gate, in `decisions.md` as `rejected`. The skill explains why the last one differs, but the first three overlap.
rows.recommendation: Make the spec section the record. Let the dossier link to it and keep `decisions.md` for three-test decisions only.

rows.title: The reasons behind specs reach disk late, or never
rows.detail: `spec-feature` writes the dossier once, at step 9; only glossary terms and three-test decisions land on disk while the interview runs. `experience-journeys` writes personas and the hero choice at step 7. `experience-behaviors` sends the open-question answers back into its own tables, never into the feature specs that raised them.
rows.recommendation: Open the dossier at step 2 and append to it after each step. Name the feature file that `experience-behaviors` re-runs when an answer changes a rule.

rows.title: Story stage semantics are restated in two later skills
rows.detail: `experience-journeys` defines what each stage means and says it sets priority. `spec-featuresets` restates the stage → priority mapping in step 4, and `experience-shell` restates the stage → navigation prominence rule in step 2. `spec-featuresets` consumes `candidate_features` by name and does not restate it.
rows.recommendation: Let `experience-journeys` own the stage definitions. Cite them in the two later skills.

rows.title: The shell names navigation targets before any screen exists
rows.detail: All three flows that contain `experience-shell` run it before `spec-feature`. The shell declares destinations as screen ids "they will get" and accepts unresolved targets with a warning, so the nav is a guess that the feature loop may contradict.
rows.recommendation: Run the shell after the feature loop and derive its nav from the screens that exist. Or derive the nav from the featureset roster only.

rows.title: Two mockup renderers draw the same screens and journeys
rows.detail: Both skills hard-gate `07_screens` and render one page per screen plus one click path per journey. `mockup-feedback` edits the screen specs but regenerates nothing: it names `mockup-walkthrough` as the next run, and neither `mockup-feedback` nor `mockup-annotate` mentions storybook (measured with grep). After a feedback round the storybook goes stale.
rows.recommendation: Let the walkthrough own the journeys. Reduce storybook to the component layer, or let it read the walkthrough manifest.

rows.title: The annotation category enum lives in five places, one schema copied twice
rows.detail: `session.schema.json` is byte-identical in `mockup-annotate/references/` and `mockup-feedback/references/` (1,503 bytes each). The four categories also appear in the overlay script, in `patch-format.md`, and in the prose of `mockup-annotate` step 6. `triage.schema.json` does not carry the enum.
rows.recommendation: Keep one `session.schema.json` that both skills reference. Let prose and templates cite it and never list the values.

rows.title: `mockup-feedback` edits screen specs under no contract section
rows.detail: `contracts/README.md` lists `mockup-feedback` as a reader of `feedback_loop.md`, but the skill cites no contract and the contract has no section for it. Its patches rewrite screen specs and promote provisional element ids. The protocol covers `experience-journeys`, `spec-featuresets`, `spec-feature`, `architecture-datamodel`, behaviors and `build-implement`.
rows.recommendation: Add a `mockup-feedback` section to `feedback_loop.md` covering screen edits and id promotion. Cite it at step 4 of the skill.

rows.title: `mockup-walkthrough` opens about nine inputs before it renders
rows.detail: By the end of step 3 the skill has read the onboarding file, the scope file, the devlog, the screen specs, the tokens, the stories, the feature specs, `RENDERER.md` and the 445-line renderer contract. It also lists four reference items, though one renderer needs only its own.
rows.recommendation: List only the references of the renderer the project resolves. Move the devlog check into the renderer reference.

rows.title: The data-model skill writes the model first and pins vocabulary last
rows.detail: Step 1 reads the glossary for "words already pinned", steps 3–5 write the model, step 6 writes the glossary, and step 8 asks for approval and then says "Then write" after the files already exist. The skill calls itself the only step that holds the whole vocabulary at once.
rows.recommendation: Pin the vocabulary before step 3. Move the approval ahead of every write.

rows.title: architecture-datamodel reads architecture.md without declaring it
rows.detail: Step 1 reads `10_blueprint/architecture.md` for module entities, but the prerequisites and `artifacts.requires` do not list it; only `06_behaviors` is declared (soft). `concept_structure.md` puts stack-specific schema files such as `schema.prisma` under `datamodel/`. The skill defers that translation to `build-database`, which takes the schema location from the template.
rows.recommendation: Declare `architecture.md` as a soft prerequisite of `architecture-datamodel`. Name one owner for the stack-specific schema file in `concept_structure.md`.

rows.title: External integrations are recorded in techstack.md and architecture.md
rows.detail: `architecture-techstack` writes `## Additional Integrations` (payments, mail, file storage) and shows the outside services at approval. `architecture-system` then asks about external services in step 3 and records them as `external_integrations`; its step 1 reads `techstack.md` only for `tech_stack_skill`. The `framework_experience` and `hosting` input fields repeat topics that step 3 asks again.
rows.recommendation: Give integrations one home, `architecture.md`, and drop the section from `techstack.md`. Make step 3 skip every question that an input field already answered.

rows.title: The entity-feature link is written twice: feature-map.json, data_entities[]
rows.detail: Step 5 writes `feature-map.json` (model to feature files); step 7 writes `data_entities[]` into each feature (feature to models). That is one relation in two files, and `ops-review` and `feedback_loop.md` must keep the pair in sync. Step 4 also restates `seed_data.md` rules (timestamps, locales, string lengths) after it cites the contract.
rows.recommendation: Keep `data_entities[]` as the link and derive `feature-map.json` from it, or drop the file. In step 4, cite `seed_data.md` and delete the restated rules.

rows.title: architecture-datamodel reads 7 inputs and cites 7 contracts
rows.detail: Step 1 reads the features, `brief.md`, `glossary.md`, `techstack.md`, `stories.yaml`, `architecture.md` and `06_behaviors/`. The skill cites seven contracts; only `spec-feature` also cites seven, `ops-review` cites five. The glossary reconciliation (step 6) and the feature scan come from other stages (F08, F17).
rows.recommendation: Move glossary pinning (F08) and the feature scan (F17) out of this skill. Cite contract sections, not whole files.

rows.title: Hard gates require artifacts that four profiles say they never grow
rows.detail: `cli-tool`, `api-service`, `library` and `data-pipeline` list `journeys` and `screens` under `not_grown`. `build-plan` and `build-implement` hard-gate `07_screens`; `spec-featuresets` and `quality-e2e` hard-gate `stories.yaml`. A search of `forge/` finds 0 uses of `not_grown`, so the host does not read it; in `appbuilder-mvp` no node produces `07_screens/`.
rows.recommendation: Make gates on `not_grown` artifacts `soft` and state in the step what changes without them. Add a `check.py` rule that cross-checks hard gates against `profiles/*.yaml`.

rows.title: The feature-to-commit link lives in three places, each read by another skill
rows.detail: `build-implement` step 8 writes the commits twice: in the slice `index.md` and in the spec frontmatter. `ops-review` step 8 rebuilds them from the slice dossiers into `trace.yaml`. `quality-review` reads the frontmatter copy and `quality-release` reads `trace.yaml`. The spec is also reviewed twice: `build-implement` step 3 and the Spec axis of `quality-review`.
rows.recommendation: Make `trace.yaml` the one derived join and let readers use it. Keep a single spec review, in `quality-review`.

rows.title: Two skills flip acceptance-ledger rows with no overwrite rule
rows.detail: `build-plan` creates the ledger; `build-implement` and `quality-e2e` both flip rows. `quality-review` and `ops-review` only read it. The contract says a skill flips only rows it evaluated, but not what happens when a row is already `PASS` or `FAIL`; `quality-e2e` also continues when no ledger exists.
rows.recommendation: Add a rule to the contract: the later evaluation overwrites a row and stamps its own evidence, and `FAIL` beats `PASS`. Make `quality-e2e` stop when the ledger is missing.

rows.title: build-plan names both decision files; build-branch is mostly git commands
rows.detail: `build-plan` step 1 names `10_blueprint/decisions.md` and `11_build/decisions.md` by path, which `domain_model.md` already defines. `build-branch` adds two rules to plain git: the unlanded-slice check (step 5) and the typed word for merge and discard (step 7). The other steps are git commands.
rows.recommendation: Cite `domain_model.md` in `build-plan` instead of naming both paths. State in `build-branch` that the two rules are its job.

rows.title: Database and e2e results end in chat; scaffold and branch leave only git
rows.detail: `build-database` step 9 and `quality-e2e` step 8 end with a chat report. Per-journey pass or fail reaches the ledger only through rows; screenshots stay in the codebase by design. `build-scaffold` and `build-branch` leave the scaffold approval and the chosen ending to git; ADR 0010 rejects a status file for the scaffold.
rows.recommendation: Persist the per-journey verdict where `quality-release` can read it; `quality-release` re-walks the journeys today. Leave scaffold and branch to git, as ADR 0010 says.

rows.title: quality-standards runs only in the reverse flow; build skills never read it
rows.detail: `quality-standards` appears in `skaileup-concept-reverse` and in no other flow. It says code-writing skills read its index themselves, and its example lists `build-implement` and `build-plan` as readers. Among skills only `quality-review` names `02_grounding/standards/`, so in `appbuilder-*` the index never exists and neither build skill looks for it.
rows.recommendation: Add `quality-standards` to `appbuilder-standard` after scaffold, with a step in `build-plan` and `build-implement` that reads the index. Or state that the index exists only in the reverse flow.

rows.title: ops-review is the longest skill and half of it is mechanical rule checks
rows.detail: `ops-review` has 111 lines and 12 steps, the most of any skill. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 7 check structure, frontmatter, naming and decay against rules the contracts state mechanically. Three skills then act on the same acceptance state: `ops-review` turns a failing row red, `quality-release` refuses on a red row, `quality-review` re-runs `PASS` rows.
rows.recommendation: Move the mechanical half into a `check_concept.py` that `ops-review` calls, as `scripts/check.py` does for this collection. Keep judgement and the trace in the skill.

rows.title: Release thresholds sit in the skill body, not in the evaluator contract
rows.detail: `quality-release` fixes design average >= 7, accessibility >= 70 and LCP under 4s in steps 6 and 7. `evaluator.md` refers to a "pass threshold" and a "failure floor" and gives no number. The contract also says a skill that pins its own version of a rule will disagree with itself.
rows.recommendation: Move the numeric thresholds to a table in `contracts/evaluator.md` and cite it at step 7.

rows.title: identity.md contract lists tone; design-brand disclaims tone
rows.detail: `concept_structure.md` says `identity.md` holds colours, fonts, tone and copy guidelines. `design-brand` says copy and tone of voice are not its job, and its step 5 lists no tone. No skill claims tone, so the contract names a content that nobody writes.
rows.recommendation: Write one sentence in `concept_structure.md` that names who owns tone and copy, or remove them from the `identity.md` line.

rows.title: skaileup finds the next skill by scanning the tree, not by lookup
rows.detail: Step 3.2 walks the flow and picks "the first node whose artifacts are not yet in the tree". Flow nodes carry only `skill`, `label` and `phase`; no skill and no flow declares what it produces. The router must open each skill to learn what its output looks like.
rows.recommendation: Resolve through the `produces` list of F05: the router then compares one list per node against the tree.

sections.title: Target shape
sections.sub: one hierarchy, one owner per artifact

blocks.text: The principle: one hierarchy (domain language, data model, features, screens), one owner per artifact, and every decision of the user lands in a markdown file that the editor opens ([[F08]], [[F17]], [[F13]]).
Proposed order of the standard flow:

items: [[concept-scope]] and [[concept-onboard]]: `answers.json` is the one record of every answer ([[F06]], [[F16]]).
Domain language (new): `_concept/glossary.md`, first level, one writer. Every later skill reads it first ([[F08]], [[F30]]).
[[concept-research]] runs alongside, before brand and journeys ([[F12]]).
[[experience-journeys]]: stories use glossary terms and carry no `candidate_entities` ([[F18]]).

Data model: [[architecture-datamodel]] moves ahead of the features (`10_blueprint/datamodel/`, conceptually `05_datamodel/`). It names entities from the glossary only, and `feature-map.json` goes ([[F17]], [[F33]]).
[[spec-featuresets]] and [[experience-behaviors]] read the entities and never coin names ([[F18]], [[F19]]).
Feature loop with [[spec-feature]]: spec and screens. The dossier opens at step 2 ([[F23]]).
[[experience-shell]] runs after the loop. Navigation comes from real screens ([[F25]]).
[[mockup-walkthrough]] is the one mockup renderer, then [[mockup-annotate]] and [[mockup-feedback]] ([[F26]]).

blocks.text: One owner per artifact. The first 14 rows are the artifact targets; the other rows are files that today have several writers or no home.

rows: One file for competitor knowledge, shared with `research/competitors.md` ([[F10]]).
One owner per subfolder: `onboarding/`, `research/` and `findings/`, `standards/`. Screenshots live in `findings/` only ([[F11]]).
Stories carry the criterion id; spec and ledger cite it ([[F20]]).
The feature spec has one owner. The data model no longer writes into it ([[F17]], [[F33]]).
Permissions move to the feature spec ([[F19]]).
Shell runs after the loop ([[F25]]). Feedback patches through the contract ([[F28]]).
Open at step 2, append per step ([[F23]]).
One owner per file. `glossary.md` leaves the folder ([[F08]]).
One owner per subfolder or file: `slices/` and `acceptance-criteria/`, `reviews/`, `trace.yaml`, `release.yaml` ([[F36]], [[F37]]).
New: first-level file, written by one domain-language step after the brief; every later writer reads it ([[F08]]).
The record of every answer and approval; seeded from the host's `_grounding/<step>/user_input.json` ([[F06]], [[F13]]).
`build-plan` owns the rows; the others flip a `status` field ([[F37]]).
The single trace of feature to code ([[F36]]).
